issues.legal_issue: The annual value of rent-controlled premises for municipal property-tax assessment is limited by the fair rent determinable under the applicable rent-control law when the municipal law neither overrides that law nor independently prescribes the valuation method.
material_facts: The property was a building let to tenants on agreed rent, but no fair rent had been fixed under the applicable tenancy law.

The municipal law valued property by the rent it could reasonably be expected to command and contained neither an overriding clause nor an independent method displacing the tenancy law’s fair-rent measure.
The High Court had treated the actual contractual rent as the basis for valuation.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was wrong to make actual contractual rent the general basis of annual valuation; the municipal law must be read with the tenancy law, and the annual value is limited to the fair rent determinable under that law.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 168 of the Calcutta Municipal Act, 1951, read with Sections 4 and 8 of the West Bengal Premises Tenancy Act, 1956, annual value cannot exceed the fair rent determinable under the tenancy law. The Court applied Corporation of Calcutta v. Padma Debi, Guntur Municipal Council v. Guntur Town Rate Payers’ Association, Corporation of Calcutta v. Life Insurance Corporation, Dewan Daulat Rai Kapoor v. New Delhi Municipal Committee, Dr. Balbir Singh v. Municipal Corporation of Delhi, Morvi Municipality v. State of Gujarat, Bhagwant Rai v. State of Punjab, and New Delhi Municipal Committee v. M.N. Soi. It distinguished Municipal Corporation, Indore v. Ratna Prabha and Indian Oil Corporation Ltd. v. Municipal Corporation because the municipal law there contained an overriding clause, and Assistant General Manager, Central Bank of India v. Commissioner, Municipal Corporation for the City of Ahmedabad because that municipal law independently defined annual letting value.

predicates.municipal_property_tax_assessment: The proceeding concerns assessment of municipal property tax on a building or land.
predicates.rent_control_law_applies: The property is subject to a rent-control regime that governs the rent recoverable from a tenant.
predicates.municipal_law_has_no_override: The applicable municipal law contains neither an overriding rule displacing the rent-control measure nor an independent method for determining annual value.

issues.definition: When a municipal property-tax assessment concerns rent-controlled property and the municipal law has no overriding or independent valuation rule, the annual value is limited to the fair rent that can be determined.

issues.legal_issue: Agreed rent is the fair-rent measure for municipal valuation while the tenancy law’s initial agreed-rent deeming window applies.
material_facts: The building had been constructed and let, but the assessing authority had not determined when it was first let.
The tenancy law’s proviso treated the rent agreed when the premises were first let as fair rent during an initial period.
The Court held that the first letting date had to be determined to establish whether that treatment applied.
issues.conclusion: If the initial agreed-rent deeming window applies, the agreed rent must be used as the fair-rent basis for annual value; the assessing authority must determine when the property was first let before making the fresh assessment.
issues.legal_principle: The proviso to Section 8(1)(d) of the West Bengal Premises Tenancy Act, 1956, deems the rent agreed when premises are first let to be fair rent during the specified initial period. Because municipal annual value is determined by reference to fair rent under Section 168 of the Calcutta Municipal Act, 1951, that deemed fair rent is the relevant measure during that window.

predicates.municipal_property_tax_assessment: The proceeding concerns assessment of municipal property tax on a building or land.
predicates.initial_agreed_rent_window_applies: The premises were first let and the tenancy law treats the rent agreed at that first letting as fair rent for the period currently being assessed.

issues.definition: If an assessment falls within the tenancy law’s initial agreed-rent window, the annual value uses the rent agreed when the premises were first let.

issues.legal_issue: After the tenancy law’s initial agreed-rent deeming window ends, municipal annual value is based on the fair rent calculated under its cost-based measure.
material_facts: The tenancy law provided a cost-based method for calculating fair rent for premises constructed and let after that law commenced.
The Court held that after the initial agreed-rent treatment ceased to apply, annual value had to be determined under that cost-based method.
The date of first letting was unknown, so the assessing authority had to establish whether the initial window had ended.
issues.conclusion: Once the initial agreed-rent deeming window has ended, the annual value must be determined using the cost-based fair-rent measure in the tenancy law.
issues.legal_principle: Section 8(1)(d) of the West Bengal Premises Tenancy Act, 1956, provides a cost-based formula for fair rent for qualifying premises, including the cost of construction, the land’s market price at commencement of construction, and a share of municipal rates and taxes. Read with Section 168 of the Calcutta Municipal Act, 1951, that fair rent is the basis for annual value after the proviso’s agreed-rent treatment ceases to apply.

predicates.municipal_property_tax_assessment: The proceeding concerns assessment of municipal property tax on a building or land.
predicates.rent_control_law_applies: The property is subject to a rent-control regime that provides a method for determining fair rent.
predicates.initial_agreed_rent_window_has_ended: The period during which the rent agreed at first letting is treated as fair rent has ended.

issues.definition: When rent-controlled property is assessed after its initial agreed-rent window, its annual value uses the cost-based fair-rent measure.
